A random variable $X$ has the probability distribution given below.

| $x$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $0.25$ | $0.35$ | $0.4$ |

Calculate $\text{E}[{X}^{4}].$

examples.knowledge_point: Calculating Higher Moments of a Random Variable
examples.problem:
A random variable $X$ has the probability distribution given below.

| $x$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $0.15$ | $0.25$ | $0.5$ | $0.1$ |

Calculate $\textrm E[X^3].$
examples.worked_solution:
If $X$ is a discrete random variable with probability mass function $f(x)$ and sample space $S,$ the expected value of $X^3$ is given by

$$
\textrm E[X^3] = \sum\limits_{x \in S} x^3 \cdot f(x).
$$

Summing up the products of each cubed value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{3}] & ={\sum }_{x\in S}{x}^{3}\cdot f(x) \\  & ={1}^{3}\cdot 0.15+{2}^{3}\cdot 0.25+{3}^{3}\cdot 0.5+{4}^{3}\cdot 0.1 \\  & =1\cdot 0.15+8\cdot 0.25+27\cdot 0.5+64\cdot 0.1 \\  & =0.15+2+13.5+6.4 \\  & =22.05.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
A random variable $X$ has the probability distribution given below.

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}, & x=4 \\ \frac{1}{3}, & x=5 \\ \frac{1}{6}, & x=6\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$
feedback.worked_solution:
If $X$ is a discrete random variable with probability mass function $f(x)$ and sample space $S,$ the expected value of ${X}^{2}$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{2}]={\sum }_{x\in S}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x).
$$

Summing up the products of each squared value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\sum }_{x\in S}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x) \\  & ={4}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2}+{5}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{3}+{6}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{6} \\  & =8+\frac{25}{3}+6 \\  & =\frac{67}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
